title: Analytics contract
description: What the app's product analytics collects and where it goes. check-analytics.mjs compares it with the event catalog, the adapter and app.config.ts; scripts/analytics/analytics-manifest.ts turns `collects` into the iOS privacy manifest entries and the Google Play Data safety rows. Raise ANALYTICS_CONSENT_VERSION whenever `collects`, `sdk` or `endpoints` change.

sdk.description: The npm package of the analytics SDK, imported only by src/services/analytics/<vendor>-analytics-adapter.ts; "none" while the app has the port and catalog but no vendor yet.

audience.description: general, or child-directed (Kids Category, Play Families): then no third-party analytics SDK at all until the developer's own review allows one (App Review 1.3 and 5.1.4).

tracking.description: true only when analytics links its data with third-party data for advertising or advertising measurement, or shares it with a data broker (Apple's definition). Then Apple's ATT answer decides isTrackingAllowed and the data types it covers say tracking: true. Default false: analytics never tracks.

identifies.description: true when the app sends an account id with events (identify). Default false: analytics is anonymous. true requires a user-id entry in collects, linked.

endpoints.description: Every https origin the SDK sends to, region chosen on purpose (the privacy audit allows exactly these). The adapter's host comes from ANALYTICS_HOST, which must be one of them.

consent.description: The consent question this collection was asked under: version equals ANALYTICS_CONSENT_VERSION in src/services/analytics/analytics-consent.ts, and covers is the fingerprint of sdk, endpoints and collects taken when that version was set (check-analytics consent-covers prints the current value). A changed collection raises both and records the new fingerprint.

collects.description: Every data type analytics sends off the device, with the store-declaration answers. Drives NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes and the Data safety form.

linked.description: Linked to the user's identity through their account, device or other details (Apple). A persisted install id links the data to the device: true unless the developer's privacy review says otherwise.

why.description: One line a reviewer reads: what in the app produces this data.
